claim_assessments.decisive_argument: The full commutant and complete reducibility give H_k=sum W_tau tensor U_tau with D_k=product M_s(k). The connected center acts scalarly on each W_tau, so it remains derived-irreducible. D-module dimensions give quaternionic 2f|g and Type-IV fb^2|g; polarization factoring beta_W tensor b_U gives Type-I/II alternating and Type-III symmetric column forms. Positivity distinguishes the quaternionic adjoint signs. In Type III the proof uses two multiplicity lines with nonzero pairing and a matrix-unit transport, not the zero restriction twice to one line. Type IV has perfect opposite-embedding pairs. All maps and pairings remain Hodge in every scalar conjugate. Averaging a Riemann form preserves positivity and makes a quadratic action compatible, but does not make the Hermitian form hyperbolic.

claim_assessments.decisive_argument: Every Galois orbit of simple derived ideals has a nonzero circle projection somewhere, or its rational adjoint kernel contradicts minimality. At an active simultaneous conjugate, fixing the other tensor factors gives a nonzero semisimple traceless operator with exactly two eigenvalues on the chosen factor. A nonminuscule highest weight has a three-step positive-root string. A Weyl conjugate of the operator makes that root nonzero, producing three eigenvalues without changing its spectrum, a contradiction. Transport back proves the conclusion without assuming the original column is mixed.

claim_assessments.exact_scope: Dimension at most six with a unital imaginary-quadratic action, arbitrary actual periods, full endomorphism algebras and admissible matrix-copy identifications. Types I/II have symplectic ranks 2,4,6; III has g=4 or 6, f=r=1 and SO_g; IV has field center K and standard SL_a columns, either nonembedded E with (f,g,r,a)=(1,3,2,3), or embedded E with f=1,3<=a=g<=6 or (f,a,g)=(2,2,4),(2,3,6),(3,2,6). Rank-two IV has both pure and mixed pairs.
claim_assessments.decisive_argument: A unital field action restricts injectively to each isotypic factor. In Type I the field F tensor E forces even multiplicity; quaternionic divisibilities give the other bounds and exclude symmetric rank two. In IV all-pure and rank-one cases are CM. A rank-two column mixed in every conjugate would give an all-conjugate alternating pair and hence a forbidden cross-center commutant map. The sole b>1 numerical case (4,1,2,2) is therefore excluded. For a field center, nonsplit K tensor E forces even multiplicity, leaving only the repeated quadratic-center threefold. Split idempotent ranks may be zero, so noncentral repeated actions are included. The small minuscule table gives the images; in quadratic center, derived self-duality gives a forbidden zero-shift opposite intertwiner, while the sole nonselfdual composite 2 tensor 3 has distinct Lie types and cannot be one active Galois orbit. Actual-group restriction onto each factor is surjective by minimality.

An invertible intertwiner translates the source circle spectrum by its character; translation preserving {-1,1} is zero. Repeat separately for every scalar conjugate. claim_assessments.decisive_argument: A semisimple subdirect algebra in simple targets is a product of graph-diagonal source ideals, with a Galois-invariant link equivalence relation. Ordinary mixed links contradict AG-DESCENT. The partially pure target sets over one E-embedding have transitive prime sizes 2 or 3, so a link relation is discrete or universal; universal linkage contradicts zero derived circle differential at a pure column and nonzero differential at a mixed column. Only the quartic fourfold has room for an external non-CM target, at most one Galois-stable A1; a link to either internal conjugate would link both. In SO4, the 2 tensor 2 spectrum permits exactly one active ideal, so minimality forces the two ideals to be interchanged by Galois, excluding external links in the same way. SO6's wedge-square SL4 representation cannot coexist with an SL4 standard partner because the Type III sixfold exhausts the budget. The necessary 3-cycle also exists for a non-Galois degree-three action.
